headline: Tram Tickets and Courthouse Access
reservation: Tram tickets to the top of the Arch frequently sell out and should be reserved well in advance through the official partner site. Entry to the Museum and Visitor Center is generally open, but specific tours of the Old Courthouse may have separate requirements. Always check the official NPS site for current construction impacts on courthouse access.

days.title: Engineering and Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Downtown St. Louis

stops.name: Gateway Arch Tram
stops.detail: Ascend the 630-foot stainless steel monument for panoramic views of the Mississippi River and city skyline.

stops.name: The Museum under the Arch
stops.detail: Explore interactive galleries detailing the history of westward expansion and indigenous cultures.

days.driving: Walking within park grounds; 25-minute drive from airport
days.note: Tram pods are small and enclosed; consider this if you have discomfort with tight spaces.

days.title: History and Riverfront Paths

stops.name: Old Courthouse
stops.detail: Visit the site of the Dred Scott case and learn about the legal history of American civil rights.

stops.name: Riverfront Trail
stops.detail: Walk the paved paths along the Mississippi to see the monument's scale from the water's edge.

days.driving: Walking between downtown sites; local street parking required
days.note: The Old Courthouse may have varying hours due to ongoing preservation projects; verify before visiting.

days.title: Urban Nature and Reflections

stops.name: North and South Reflection Ponds
stops.detail: Photograph the Arch's reflection in these manicured water features within the park landscaping.

stops.name: Explorer's Garden
stops.detail: Stroll through native plantings that showcase the flora of the Missouri river region.

days.driving: Local transfer; allow 15 minutes for city traffic
days.note: The park grounds are open late, but museum and tram services follow specific daily hours.

intel.title: City Garages
intel.text: There is no dedicated park parking lot; visitors must use downtown St. Louis garages or street meters. Check for event-related closures if visiting during a home game at nearby Busch Stadium.

intel.title: Urban Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is excellent throughout the park and museum. Use the official NPS app to access digital tours and site history while walking the grounds.

intel.title: Metropolitan Services
intel.text: Fuel stations are widely available throughout the St. Louis metro area. Ensure your vehicle is fueled before entering the downtown core to avoid navigating narrow city streets.

intel.title: Security Screening
intel.text: All visitors to the Arch must pass through a security checkpoint similar to airport protocols. Allow at least 30 minutes for this process during busy weekend hours.

intel.title: Paved Mobility
intel.text: The park features over five miles of fully paved and accessible trails. These paths connect the monument to the riverfront and the historic downtown business district.

plan.arrival: Rental pickup at St. Louis Lambert (STL) followed by a short drive to a downtown hotel for check-in before walking to the Arch Visitor Center.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are ideal for city navigation; RVs should be parked at designated outskirts lots due to height and turn restrictions downtown.
plan.goldenHour: The Riverfront Trail offers prime sunset views as the light reflects off the stainless steel Arch legs.
